title: Directed writing
examples: If I have an article, how do I change it into a speech?
What is the main difference between writing for a newspaper and writing for a speech?
Do I have to keep all the information from the original text?

explain.say: Today we are learning to change one type of writing into another.

items: Process: Analyze and adapt the content

explain.say: First, you must identify the original text's main message clearly.
Next, consider who you are writing for; this is your audience.
Then, change the tone and style to fit your new goal.
For example, an article about recycling can become a speech.
In everyday life, think about explaining a complex process to a child.

faq.q: Do I have to use every single piece of information from the source text?
faq.a: No, you should only use the most important points that support your new purpose. You must select the key ideas.
asks: Can I leave out some facts?
Is it okay to ignore minor details?

faq.q: How do I change the tone from writing to speaking?
faq.a: Speaking requires more direct address, using 'you' often, and using rhetorical questions. It should sound natural when spoken aloud.
asks: Should I write like I am talking?
What makes writing sound like speaking?

faq.q: What is the difference between adapting and summarizing?
faq.a: Summarizing means making it shorter while keeping the original focus. Adapting means changing the way it is said for a new effect.
asks: Is adapting the same as summarizing?
Do I change the meaning when I adapt it?

faq.q: If the source text is very formal, should my new piece also be formal?
faq.a: No, if your new purpose is to persuade friends, you should make the tone much more informal and engaging.
asks: Must the tone match the source?
Can I make it sound less serious?

faq.q: What if the source text is biased?
faq.a: You must acknowledge the bias while adapting it. You can present the information fairly or challenge the bias depending on your goal.
asks: Should I point out the bias?
How do I handle biased information?

facts: Directed writing means writing for a specific purpose and audience.
The source text provides the core information, not the final structure.
When changing purpose, you must adjust the tone, vocabulary, and structure.
A speech requires direct address, using words like 'you' and 'we'.

quiz.say: A scientific report about climate change is changed into a persuasive speech for local council members. What must change most significantly?

options.show: The tone must become urgent and persuasive.
options.say: The tone must become urgent and persuasive.

options.show: The structure must remain purely academic.
options.say: The structure must remain purely academic.

quiz.why: The original report is objective, but a speech to council members needs to motivate them to act, requiring a persuasive tone.

wrong.0: The audience is crucial; knowing they are council members dictates the level of evidence and formality needed.
wrong.2: While simplification helps, the primary change is the intent (persuasion) not just the word level.
wrong.3: A speech format is different from a report format; it needs openings and closings suitable for speaking.

quiz.say: If you adapt a recipe article into a short, engaging social media caption, what element is most important to change?

options.show: The length must be drastically reduced.
options.say: The length must be drastically reduced.

options.show: You must keep all the ingredients listed.
options.say: You must keep all the ingredients listed.

options.show: The tone must remain purely instructional.
options.say: The tone must remain purely instructional.

options.show: You must use complex, formal vocabulary.
options.say: You must use complex, formal vocabulary.

quiz.why: Social media captions require very short, punchy text that is easy to read quickly on a phone screen.

wrong.1: The goal is engagement, so listing everything might be too much detail for a caption.
wrong.2: While instructional, a caption needs to be more exciting or attention-grabbing than just instructions.
wrong.3: Social media generally favours casual, accessible language to connect with a broad audience.

quiz.say: A historical text describing a battle is adapted into a dramatic monologue. What is the most crucial structural change?

options.show: The length must remain the same.
options.say: The length must remain the same.

options.show: The audience must be academic historians.
options.say: The audience must be academic historians.

options.show: The focus must shift to one character's feelings.
options.say: The focus must shift to one character's feelings.

options.show: The text must become purely factual.
options.say: The text must become purely factual.

quiz.why: A monologue is a single character speaking, so the structure must narrow down the vast information to one viewpoint.

wrong.0: To focus on one character, the text usually needs to be condensed to only what that character would know or feel.
wrong.1: A monologue is designed for performance, meaning the audience connection is more important than academic accuracy alone.
wrong.3: A monologue thrives on emotion and internal thought, not just dry facts.
